methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective analysis of 136 pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1 AML patients with clearly prespecified candidate variables, LASSO with 10-fold CV for variable selection, multivariate Cox regression for independent prognostic factors, and bootstrap (500 resamples) for internal validation. Strengths include consecutive enrollment across two linked protocols (AML-CAMS-2009 and AML-CAMS-2016), standardized MRD methodology with RT-qPCR (assay sensitivity 10 copies, ABL threshold >=1x10^5 copies), and X-tile for cutoff determination. Weaknesses: single-center, modest event count (22 deaths, 28 relapses) leading to EPV issues and wide CIs (authors acknowledge), treatment regimen is confounded with calendar time since protocol assignment was based on enrollment period, and HSCT was not modeled as time-dependent exposure. No external validation performed; only internal bootstrap.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study using prospective protocol-enrolled patients classifies as Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate: nomograms predicting 3-year OS and RFS in pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML could support individualized post-remission decision-making, and High-Risk MRD as a combined biomarker is actionable. However, the absence of external validation limits immediate clinical deployment; authors appropriately state that prospective multicenter validation is required.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD applies to this prediction model development and internal validation study. The manuscript reports many TRIPOD items: cohort definition, outcome definitions, predictor measurement, model building approach (LASSO + Cox), performance metrics (AUC, calibration, DCA, C-index), and internal validation by bootstrap. Missing or incomplete items: explicit TRIPOD checklist reference, detailed handling of missing data beyond brief mention of random forest imputation, sample size justification relative to events-per-variable guidance, no external validation, and no formal data or code availability statement. Institutional clinical data typically restricted.

novelty_literature.justification: Nomograms for AML outcomes are not novel per se (many prior examples), and WBC, MRD, EMI, BM blasts are individually well-established prognostic factors. The novel contributions are (1) focus on the specific pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1 subtype in a Chinese cohort, (2) the combined High-Risk MRD definition integrating post-induction transcript reduction with post-consolidation MRD (already published by the same group as ref 14), and (3) comparison across the AML-CAMS-2009 vs 2016 protocols. Meaningful incremental contribution to pediatric AML prognostication.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally clear with structured methods and results. Tables and figures are described appropriately. Some awkward phrasing in places ('link to treatment-tolerant subclones'), occasional redundancy between results and discussion, and the abstract lacks a formal background/methods/results structure at its opening (immediately starts with objective). Overall readable but not polished.

key_strengths: Consecutive enrollment of pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML from two sequential standardized protocols (AML-CAMS-2009 and 2016)
LASSO variable selection with 10-fold CV and multivariate Cox regression with internal bootstrap validation (500 resamples)
Strong discrimination (C-index 0.842 OS, 0.789 RFS) and calibration with decision curve analysis included
Standardized RT-qPCR MRD methodology with defined sensitivity thresholds
High-Risk MRD composite definition (suboptimal induction response + post-consolidation MRD >=0.01%) provides integrated prognostic biomarker
key_concerns: Single-center cohort with modest events (22 deaths, 28 relapses) limits precision and external generalizability
Treatment regimen confounded with calendar time; AML-CAMS-2016 patients also benefited from temporal improvements in supportive care
No external validation performed; only internal bootstrap
HSCT not modeled as time-dependent covariate, leaving residual confounding
Genomic profiling limited to KIT and RAS mutations; co-mutation patterns not assessed
No data or analysis code availability statement
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent single-center prediction model development with appropriate statistical framework and internal validation but limited external validity and residual confounding of treatment regimen with calendar time place the work at Tier 3 with minor revisions needed for TRIPOD completeness.
